entry.title: Binance CFO Kaiser Ng steps down days after hackers steal $6.3-billion
entry.summary:
Binance CFO Kaiser Ng has resigned, with Justin Yek, former financial vice president at payments platform Airwallex, appointed as his successor. The leadership change was announced days after a security incident on October 29, 2026, in which approximately $6.3 billion in digital assets were stolen from the exchange.
The resignation of a key financial executive following the largest crypto theft on record raises questions about internal accountability and financial stewardship at the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange.
Binance co-CEO Yi He stated that a transition plan for Ng's departure had been in place for the past six months, preceding the hack. The company has stated that user losses from the hack will be covered.

entry.title: Circle freezes $1.1B in USDC after Binance hack, blocking funds at specific addresses.
entry.summary:
Following a major hack on the Binance exchange in October 2026, Circle has frozen $1.1 billion worth of its USDC stablecoin in specific blockchain addresses linked to the incident.
This action prevents the immediate movement of a significant portion of the stolen funds, potentially aiding in their recovery and demonstrating the centralized control stablecoin issuers can exert in response to security breaches.
The Binance hack, which occurred on 29 October 2026, resulted in a loss of approximately $6.3 billion. Circle's freeze is part of a broader response that has reportedly seen around $3 billion in stolen assets frozen across various entities.

entry.title: India Flags AI-Assisted Campaign as South Korea Urges Exchange Security After Binance Hack
entry.summary:
South Korean regulators have urged cryptocurrency exchanges to bolster their security measures following a major hack targeting Binance. Separately, Indian authorities have flagged concerns about the use of artificial intelligence in a political campaign.
The regulatory calls for enhanced security come directly in response to a significant security breach at a leading global exchange, which could impact user funds and market stability. The Indian warning highlights growing regulatory scrutiny over the use of AI in sensitive areas like political campaigning.
The Binance hack reportedly involved $6.3 billion, according to web search results. Binance co-CEO Yi He stated that a subsequent executive transition had been planned for months and was not a direct response to the hack.

entry.title: Keplr Wallet social login accounts experience unauthorized transactions; Web3Auth suspends embedded wallet service due to security issue
entry.summary:
On November 7, 2026, Web3Auth announced a security issue in its service, leading to unauthorized transactions for some Keplr Wallet accounts created via Google or Apple social logins. Web3Auth has suspended its embedded wallet service, and both teams are conducting a joint investigation.
The incident directly compromises user assets in affected wallets, prompting Keplr to advise users with Google or Apple login accounts to stop deposits and move remaining liquid assets. The service suspension also disrupts the onboarding functionality for applications relying on Web3Auth's embedded wallets.
Keplr's preliminary assessment indicates accounts created with a recovery phrase or hardware wallet are unaffected. Web3Auth's initial investigation found no impact on MetaMask users. The exact number of affected accounts and the amounts stolen have not been quantified.

entry.title: Zero-click iOS exploits drain $4M USDT from active TRON wallets
entry.summary:
A zero-click iOS exploit has been used to steal approximately $4 million in USDT from active TRON wallets, with blockchain analysis firm Bitquery tracing the theft across 365 TRON addresses between October 30 and November 4, 2026.
This incident highlights a sophisticated attack vector where users can be compromised without any interaction, directly threatening the security of self-custodied crypto assets on mobile devices.
The theft included 89 addresses where only TRX was stolen. Most of the devices and specific exploits used in the attacks remain unidentified.

entry.title: Binance France To Close Customer Accounts on December 31, Introduce Monthly Fees From November 29
entry.summary:
Binance France will close all customer accounts on December 31, 2026, after failing to obtain authorization under the EU's MiCA framework, and will begin charging a monthly custody fee of 0.025% on assets held from November 29, 2026.
This marks Binance's complete operational exit from the French market, forcing users to withdraw assets or face fees and potential asset conversion after the deadline.
Deposits are already suspended. The monthly fee has a minimum charge of 10 USDC, with the first deduction occurring within three days after November 29. Assets not withdrawn by December 31 may be treated as inactive and converted or transferred per Binance's Terms of Service.

entry.title: Loopscale Reopens All Vaults After Attack-Related Freeze
entry.summary: Loopscale has reopened all its vaults, including the USDC Genesis Vault, and lifted remaining loan-management restrictions following a security incident.

entry.title: Bitcoin ETFs flip negative for 2026 after $1.28 billion outflow week, worst since June
entry.summary:
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs experienced $1.28 billion in net outflows last week, marking the largest weekly withdrawal since June 2026. This outflow has turned the cumulative net flows for the year 2026 negative.
The scale of the outflow, the worst in over four months, signals a significant shift in institutional capital movement and sentiment towards these regulated investment products.
The report cites data from Farside Investors, a provider of ETF flow tracking. The previous record weekly outflows occurred in June 2026, when monthly outflows reached approximately $4.5 billion.

entry.title: Bitcoin Core Developer Proposes Quantum Attack Collateral Defense Scheme
entry.summary:
Bitcoin Core developer Cory Fields has proposed a 'quantum mine' scheme that would require collateral and a waiting period for moving bitcoins from wallets vulnerable to future quantum attacks. Legitimate owners could reclaim their assets and seize the attacker's collateral by revealing a pre-prepared proof of ownership during the waiting period.
The proposal represents a concrete, forward-looking defense mechanism against a potential future threat to Bitcoin's security model, specifically targeting the vulnerability of old wallets with exposed public keys.
The scheme would also require legitimate owners moving vulnerable coins to post collateral, as the blockchain cannot distinguish them from attackers. For dormant assets with lost keys, Fields proposed a challengeable auction mechanism.

entry.title: Coinbase Cites Split-Key Cold Storage After Binance $6.4B Hack
entry.summary:
In the wake of a reported $6.4 billion hack at Binance, Coinbase pointed to its split-key cold storage design and stated that 99% of customer assets are held in cold storage. The disclosure was framed as the industry re-examines custody security and key management.
The remarks shift attention to how exchanges architect key management, which is central to how customers and counterparties gauge custodial risk at a major venue.
Reports on the incident differ on magnitude, describing a $6.3 billion or $6.4 billion breach. Binance's own initial findings said about $6.34 billion of digital assets were affected in the Oct. 29 incident and that 98% of the impacted tokens had been replenished as of Oct. 31, verifiable on its proof-of-reserves page.

entry.title: Riot Signs $28 Billion AI Lease for Entire Corsicana Campus
entry.summary:
Riot Platforms signed a 15-year data center lease covering the entirety of its Corsicana, Texas campus — 910 MW of critical IT capacity — at roughly $28 billion in total contract value and about $1.8 billion in average annual rent including escalators. The tenant, identified as Anthropic in the company's quarterly filing, will own and operate the computing equipment while Riot supplies land and power infrastructure originally developed for Bitcoin mining.
The deal lifts Riot's total contracted data center capacity to 1,151 MW and about $38 billion in long-term contract revenue across three leases signed this year. CEO Jason Les said that at full deployment of currently executed deals, nearly all of Riot's expected cash flow will come from long-term leases with AI players rather than from Bitcoin mining, and the shares rose more than 13% on the announcement.
Riot estimates total project capital costs at $5.5 billion, to be financed primarily through debt backed by lease payments, though that financing has not yet been secured. First-phase delivery is expected in September 2027 with rent payments starting within 60 days of delivery, and Les said Bitcoin mining at Corsicana could begin winding down in summer 2027. In the third quarter Riot sold 10,599 BTC, cutting holdings from 11,380 at end-June to 2,418 at end-September, and it sold 20,264 BTC over the first nine months for about $1.5 billion.

entry.title: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa Confirms Cyberattack After ZachXBT Ties It to $133M Crypto Theft
entry.summary:
French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed in a statement to Decrypt on Wednesday that it was hit by a cyberattack that enabled fraudulent operations, saying the incident is "closed and now under control" and that operations are resuming gradually. The confirmation came one day after onchain investigator ZachXBT publicly named the bank as the alleged victim of a crypto theft exceeding $133 million.
The bank said it alerted the relevant supervisory authorities as soon as it detected the attack and temporarily suspended some transactions as a precaution. ZachXBT accused the institution of failing to make a "proper incident disclosure," which he said prevented law enforcement from freezing some $30 million in stolen funds.
Crédit Mutuel Arkéa did not mention crypto or state how much was taken, saying the affected amounts are still being assessed but are "in any event not of a nature to call into question the solidity and financial health of the group"; it said customer assets were unaffected and some transfers were only delayed. ZachXBT initially flagged more than $106 million in withdrawals from exchange accounts on November 1, later added $27 million, published four Ethereum addresses, and said he could state "with a high degree of confidence" the attacker is not the Lazarus Group.

entry.title: BitMart founder says security team ‘severely understaffed’ after new hack
entry.summary:
BitMart confirmed a new hack on Monday, and founder Sheldon Xia said in a post on X on Wednesday that the exchange's security team is "currently severely understaffed" following restructuring. Xia described the amount involved as small without disclosing a figure, while blockchain analytics firm Bitquery identified approximately $391,000 in suspicious transfers from wallets mostly associated with BitMart across three blockchains.
Bitquery traced the funds to a wallet also implicated in the more than $46 million Mercado Bitcoin hack on Monday, Nov. 2, supporting Xia's preliminary suspicion of a possible connection between the two incidents.
Xia said threats against employees and alleged retaliation by former staff had complicated efforts to retain technical personnel. Cointelegraph said it had contacted BitMart for details on the restructuring, security staffing and the latest breach but had not received a response by publication.

entry.title: Strategy raises $5.4B but barely buys bitcoin
entry.summary:
Strategy raised $5.4 billion through at-the-market common stock sales between July and September but spent only $588 million of that on bitcoin — less than 11 cents of every dollar raised. The company also sold 5,552 of its own BTC for $348.6 million, partly to fund dividends and partly to repurchase its STRC preferred stock.
The disclosure breaks a pattern: in 2024 essentially every ATM dollar became bitcoin, and even in the anomalous third quarter of 2025 more than 94 cents of each dollar still bought BTC. The shift matters because Strategy is the largest corporate bitcoin treasury, so the share of its fundraising that reaches spot BTC purchases is a directly observable demand channel.
Strategy bought 7,218 BTC during the quarter and, after accounting for its sales, ended with just 1,666 more coins than it started with. In the reporting week of October 26, $164 million of fresh MSTR dilution saw only 40 cents of each dollar go toward BTC.

entry.title: Stripe Lets US Businesses Send Stablecoins to Wallets in 160-Plus Markets
entry.summary:
Stripe launched a public preview that lets US businesses send USDC or Open USD to wallets in more than 160 markets, with transfers funded from a Treasury balance. Businesses based in New York are excluded from the preview.
The preview extends Stripe's stablecoin offering beyond holding balances in Treasury to sending funds directly to external wallets across borders, giving US business customers a new payout channel denominated in stablecoins.
The preview supports only two stablecoins, USDC and Open USD, and transfers are funded from a Treasury balance. New York-based businesses are excluded.

entry.title: Blast L2 Officially Shuts Down; Users Can Reclaim Remaining Assets via Official Website Until November 4, 2027
entry.summary:
Blast announced on X that its L2 network has formally shut down. Users still holding ETH or USD in L2 wallets, in pending withdrawals, or in Blast Mobile can reclaim their assets through the Blast official website, which will remain available for 12 months with a final support date of November 4, 2027.
The asset-recovery site is time-limited, with November 4, 2027 set as the last supported date. Earlier reporting indicated that Blast's standard withdrawal interface closed on October 26, after which users must interact directly with Ethereum bridge contracts to move assets.

entry.title: Circle earnings call: developing Arc Sectors, payments sector targeting over 100,000 TPS
entry.summary:
On its Q3 earnings call, Circle said it is developing "Arc Sectors" for its Arc chain — dedicated lanes for different types of financial activity, including a privacy sector for institutions with selective confidentiality and disclosure, a payments sector targeting more than 100,000 transactions per second, and an AI Agent sector with identity verification and audit trails. Circle expects AI agents to be discoverable, hireable, payable and trusted on Arc by the first quarter of 2027.
The disclosure pairs a concrete infrastructure roadmap with strong network metrics: Circle Payments Network annualized payment volume exceeded $58 billion, up more than 150% from $23 billion on July 31, with 205 financial institutions having joined, and Circle expects CPN to contribute meaningful revenue in 2027.
As of late October, about $1.5 billion in USDC, cirBTC and EURC was held on Arc, with over $30 billion in USDC having flowed through the chain since launch at roughly 500,000 daily transactions. In Q3, USDC accounted for 79% of stablecoin on-chain transaction volume versus 66% a year earlier, while USDC mint and redeem totaled a record $208 billion, up 42% year over year.

entry.title: Binance relied on AI to fight fraud before hackers exploited internal tool in $6 billion theft
entry.summary:
Binance's incident report described a monthslong campaign in which attackers used fake job interviews to compromise an engineer's work computer and then exploited unauthorized access to an internal wallet signing service to initiate transactions outside the normal withdrawal process. The exchange's report put the figure at roughly $6.3 billion, while coverage of the theft cited about $6 billion.
Binance said it has rebuilt the affected wallet system in a new environment in response to the incident, making the breach a direct test of how exchange-controlled signing infrastructure is secured.
According to Binance's account, the attack unfolded quickly on the evening of the theft, with the attacker reaching the internal signing service rather than the standard withdrawal path. The compromised engineer's machine also hosted an internal AI tool, which the report tied to the intrusion.

entry.title: Brazil's Biggest Bitcoin Exchange Says It Will Refund Users After a $40 Million Hack
entry.summary:
Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest crypto exchange, said it detected a security incident in one of its systems early on November 2 and froze deposits and withdrawals as a precaution, pledging to absorb the losses itself rather than pass them to customers. The exchange put the value of assets involved at about $38 million and said it had already blocked $11 million with help from Tether, Circle, Paxos, BRL1 and Chainalysis, while outside trackers estimate higher losses.
A guarantee to cover losses is only as good as the money behind it, and exchanges are not required to show customers their books, so the pledge cannot be verified from outside. Deposits and withdrawals remain suspended with no restart date, leaving users unable to move funds.
Loss estimates vary: Hypernative flagged more than $40 million in suspicious transfers across at least 10 blockchains including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and Tron; Arkham traced at least $46 million and Chainalysis about $49 million, with nearly $10 million frozen. Mercado Bitcoin said no customer lost money and no data leaked, did not say whether its $38 million figure includes the frozen amount, and has not said how attackers got in; Tether froze more than $4.5 million in USDT tied to the incident, according to CEO Paolo Ardoino.

entry.title: Update: I’ve identified an additional $27M+ of CEX withdrawals by the illicit ac
entry.summary:
An investigator posting on the Telegram channel "investigations" said they identified an additional $27M+ in centralized exchange (CEX) withdrawals by the illicit actor behind an incident whose total now exceeds $133M. According to the post, a portion of those CEX withdrawals took place after the investigator's initial disclosure.
The investigator states that the absence of a proper incident disclosure allowed $30M+ to be laundered away that EU law enforcement could otherwise have frozen. The investigator's working theory is that a large Western European financial institution was exploited and that the matter is currently being covered up — a hypothesis, not a confirmed finding.
The post lists four Ethereum addresses identified as theft addresses: 0x5cf70edce65847ef989933c3072fb0e7f335abc1, 0xe378cdccb369a64a0190577787ef61ca2eefa6b2, 0x3e6c3d135ca8f8be793e5fe1715ce6c057d140f2 and 0x99d314e6970b8d3db0dbe6f6e041cc904143400f.

entry.title: 🔍 On-chain Detective | Hacker who stole funds from an EU entity bought 27,553 ETH yesterday, worth about $62.83 million
entry.summary:
According to on-chain analyst Ai Yi (@ai_9684xtpa), a hacker suspected of stealing roughly $106 million from an EU entity bought 27,553 ETH in a single day, worth about $62.83 million, with all purchases executed on-chain at an average price of about $2,280.34; buying appears to have paused as of the Nov. 3 report.
The purchase is the largest concrete on-chain trace disclosed so far in a case where the alleged proceeds are being converted and moved rather than frozen, giving investigators and exchange compliance teams a fresh set of addresses to track.
On-chain detective ZachXBT said in a post on his personal channel that an EU entity appeared to have lost more than $106 million from accounts across multiple centralized exchanges. The hacker has been converting large amounts of USDC into ETH, moving funds to an instant exchange service to swap into Monero (XMR) via Wagyu, and bridging across multiple chains.

entry.title: Liquid: Bitcoin reserves fully restored, LBTC returns to 1:1 backing
entry.summary:
On November 3, the Liquid Federation announced that the network's Bitcoin reserves have been fully restored, re-establishing 1:1 BTC backing for all LBTC. Users can again move between bitcoin and Liquid at a 1:1 ratio through participating swap providers.
The announcement re-establishes the 1:1 peg that had been disrupted by a reserve shortfall, restoring full backing for LBTC in circulation and reopening 1:1 BTC↔Liquid transfers for users.
According to reports citing the Federation, the reserves can be publicly verified through node checks and a public dashboard. The announcement did not disclose the size of the shortfall or the remediation process.

entry.title: Tether CEO Says Company Owns Approximately 150,000 Bitcoin
entry.summary:
Speaking in a keynote at the Plan ₿ Forum in Lugano, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company owns approximately 150,000 BTC and serves more than 730 million users, adding about 30 million new wallets per quarter. He cited Tether's Q3 2026 attestation, which showed roughly $122.8 billion in directly held U.S. Treasury bills — $132.4 billion including repurchase agreements — and about $7.95 billion in excess reserves.
The remarks make public the approximate scale of Bitcoin held by the largest stablecoin issuer, alongside reserve figures that market participants track when gauging USDT's backing. It was a keynote statement rather than an announcement of a new purchase or a regulatory filing.
The figures come from Tether's Q3 2026 attestation, a periodic assurance report rather than a full audit of the company's financial statements. Ardoino also described Tether's wider Independence Stack initiative, covering energy, Bitcoin mining, peer-to-peer communications, self-custody wallets and on-device AI.

entry.title: North Korea Is Laundering Binance Hack Loot at One New Wallet Every 25 Seconds
entry.summary:
Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said in an analysis published Monday that in under four days the attacker behind the $6.43 billion Binance theft spread the funds across roughly 12,000 wallets on 11 blockchains in more than 40,000 transactions — about one new wallet every 25 seconds. Elliptic reported that about $2.85 billion, or 44% of the haul, has already been frozen or seized after Tether and Circle moved to lock up stolen stablecoins.
The 44% freeze-or-seizure rate compares with roughly 3% after North Korea's $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, according to Elliptic, which attributes the difference to stablecoin issuers acting within minutes.
Elliptic found Tether froze stolen USDT on Ethereum 37 minutes after it reached the attacker's wallet, and Circle froze all $823 million in stolen USDC before any could be swapped; about $786 million in stablecoins nonetheless escaped. The firm said the laundering is clearly automated but shows no AI decision-making, citing fixed timing, set amounts, blind retries and pauses resembling human working hours.

entry.title: Mercado Bitcoin hack losses are at $46M and growing
entry.summary:
Brazilian exchange Mercado Bitcoin suspended deposits and withdrawals on Monday after detecting a security incident in one of its systems in the early hours of the morning. Blockchain security firm Hypernative flagged more than $40 million in suspicious transfers across at least 10 blockchains, while Arkham analyst Emmett Gallic put the losses at over $46 million and said the attacker is still sweeping old deposit addresses and selling off memecoins and altcoins.
The exchange says no customer funds or data were affected, but the platform-wide suspension of deposits and withdrawals blocks all users from moving assets while funds are still being traced on-chain. Tether has frozen more than 4.5 million USDT tied to the incident, according to CEO Paolo Ardoino.
Mercado Bitcoin published attacker destination addresses on five networks — EVM chains, Bitcoin, Solana, Stellar and Tron — saying they were released so others can identify and track the funds, and it has not confirmed the $40 million-plus figure or disclosed how the attackers gained access. Hypernative's preliminary analysis spans at least 10 blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and Tron.

entry.title: ZachXBT: An EU entity suspected of having over $106 million stolen from multiple centralized exchange accounts
entry.summary:
Blockchain investigator ZachXBT warned in a Monday Telegram post that an unidentified entity in the European Union appears to have had more than $106 million drained from several centralized exchange accounts on Sunday, Nov. 1, with the funds withdrawn in USDC and USDT. Over the following 24 hours the suspected attacker swapped USDC into ETH, moved funds through instant-exchange services including WellWallet and Kyrrex, converted them into Monero (XMR) via the swap service Wagyu, and bridged assets across multiple chains; ZachXBT published 11 associated addresses.
ZachXBT said with "a high degree of confidence" that the attacker is not North Korea's Lazarus Group, setting this incident apart from the recent Binance hack. The funds were still being moved through instant-swap venues and privacy coin conversion at the time of the alert, indicating the laundering is ongoing.
The affected entity and the exchanges involved have not been publicly named, and the attacker remains unidentified. Lookonchain reported that wallet 0x9eca bought 27,553 ETH (about $62.97 million) on-chain at an average price of $2,286 as part of the fund movement.

entry.title: Arbitrum’s Security Council Can Move a Wallet’s Funds Without Its Key, Binance Freeze Shows
entry.summary:
Arbitrum's Security Council demonstrated that it can transfer funds out of a wallet without possessing that wallet's private key, in an incident tied to a freeze associated with Binance. The episode surfaced the Layer 2's emergency powers rather than a protocol exploit.
The case puts a concrete example behind long-standing questions about how much control a Layer 2's emergency multisig retains over user funds, a core decentralization and user-trust issue for Arbitrum.
Arbitrum's Security Council is a 9-of-12 multisig elected by ARB token holders that can freeze funds, pause the system and handle emergency situations, according to governance documentation and Tally's council page.

entry.title: Standard Chartered launches tokenized deposit service in Hong Kong
entry.summary:
Standard Chartered announced the launch of a tokenized deposit solution for corporate clients in Hong Kong, making the city the first market in its global network to offer the service, with plans to extend it to more markets. Built on the bank's own blockchain infrastructure and developed with support from the HKMA's distributed ledger technology regulatory incubator, the solution relies on EnsembleTX to let tokenized deposits move between participating banks in real time, with interbank settlement in central bank money — including wholesale CBDC — on a 24/7 basis.
The service is aimed at corporate clients' intra-group liquidity management and digital treasury and investment workflows, allowing tokenized deposit transfers among participating banks to be settled in central bank money around the clock.
BlockBeats reported on November 2, citing CoinDesk, that early partners include China AMC, Fireblocks and HashKey. Hong Kong is currently the only market where the bank offers the service.

entry.title: BTCPay Server: Attack surface points to version 2.4.1 and earlier, no credible hot wallet theft reports on latest release
entry.summary:
On November 2, BTCPay Server said its incident response investigation had identified an attack vector mainly targeting instances running version 2.4.1 — released July 23, 2026 — or earlier. The project said it has received no credible reports of hot wallet drains among users running the latest release, version 2.4.7, and again urged all operators to upgrade promptly.
BTCPay Server is self-hosted payment infrastructure run directly by merchants, so the exposure is concentrated among operators who have not updated past 2.4.1. BTCPay has not disclosed how many operators were affected or the value of any stolen funds.
BTCPay asked affected users to submit information and logs to its security team, and has not released technical details on how attackers accessed the wallets. Cointelegraph said it reached out to BTCPay Server for comment but received no response before publication.

entry.title: THORChain Halts Cross-Chain Swaps Over Security Flaw, Disrupting Laundering of Binance Hack Funds
entry.summary:
THORChain suspended cross-chain swaps after a security flaw was identified in the protocol. According to the report, the halt also cut off a route that had reportedly been used to move funds stolen in the Binance hack.
The halt takes a widely used decentralized cross-chain swap venue offline for users, and per the report interrupts a laundering path for stolen Binance funds.
The measure is described as a precautionary halt tied to an identified flaw rather than a confirmed exploit, and no user losses have been quantified in the report.

entry.title: THORChain: A User Voluntarily Returned 10 ETH, Treasury Solvency Restored
entry.summary:
THORChain said that on October 31 an Ethereum single-block reorganization caused the protocol to erroneously pay out 10 ETH that had never actually been received, and that the user has since voluntarily returned the 10 ETH, restoring treasury solvency. Trading remains paused across ten chains — ATOM, BCH, BSC, BTC, DOGE, ETH, LTC, SOL, TRON and ZEC — while AVAX, BASE, RUNE and XRPL remain active, pending safety checks and fixes.
The incident shows that a routine Ethereum reorg can lead to value leakage in a cross-chain protocol, and that remediation required halting trading across ten major chains. THORChain stressed that the emergency pause mechanism is controlled by node voting and does not give nodes control over assets.
The protocol's automatic solvency check triggered immediately and paused ETH swaps, and within about two minutes node operators further suspended ETH transaction signing to stop further outflows. Node operators will decide whether to re-enable each chain after confirming it is safe, and the core development team is working on fixes.

entry.title: CryptoCom to Discontinue Consumer App in Hong Kong on February 1, 2027
entry.summary:
CryptoCom will discontinue its consumer app in Hong Kong effective February 1, 2027, according to Bloomberg. The company said the move is part of efforts to optimize global operations and resource allocation, and that affected users have been notified and will receive instructions on account closures and fund withdrawals.
The shutdown removes CryptoCom's retail-facing app from Hong Kong even as the company keeps pursuing an SFC virtual asset trading platform license through Foris DAX HK Limited for its institutional exchange, leaving Hong Kong consumer users with a fixed deadline to close accounts and withdraw funds.
The consumer app closure is dated February 1, 2027, and is framed as an operational and resource-allocation decision rather than a regulatory action or insolvency event. The institutional CryptoCom Exchange business and its separate licensing application in Hong Kong are described as continuing.

entry.title: BTCPay Server Urges Shutdown After Reports of Hot-Wallet Sweeps
entry.summary:
BTCPay Server, the open-source self-hosted Bitcoin payment processor, advised operators to shut down their instances after reports that hot wallets tied to the software were being swept, indicating an active security incident affecting Bitcoin merchants. The project's guidance also directed operators to update to version 2.4.2, which refreshes LND and regenerates its admin macaroon.
Merchants running their own BTCPay instances hold the keys to the funds those servers control, so an active draining incident exposes them to direct loss until they shut down or update. BTCPay is a widely used self-hosted alternative to custodial payment processors, giving the advisory an unusually large operational footprint.
The incident appears tied to a Lightning credential flaw in versions before 2.4.2 that let attackers obtain the credentials controlling a store's Lightning funds. The project said operators unsure whether an update applied correctly should re-run it via the user interface or btcpay-update.sh; the exact loss magnitude and root cause have not been resolved in reporting.

entry.title: Cybersecurity Stocks In Focus After Binance Hack Raises Digital Asset Security Questions
entry.summary:
Simply Wall St published a market commentary item flagging cybersecurity stocks as a focus of attention after a hack at Binance renewed concerns about digital-asset security and exchange safeguards. The piece is secondary stock-market commentary rather than primary incident reporting, and it does not establish the size of the loss or the number of users affected.
The item links an exchange security failure to investor attention on listed cybersecurity vendors, framing crypto-incident risk as a potential demand driver for that sector.
Other reporting surfaced in search results describes a 2026 Binance breach as the largest-ever cryptocurrency heist, surpassing the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, with investors withdrawing $3.6 billion in funds; those figures come from separate outlets and are not part of the Simply Wall St commentary.

entry.title: b14g Suffers Unauthorized Withdrawal of 97 Million CORE, Pauses Contracts and Freezes Some Funds
entry.summary:
b14g, a Bitcoin dual-staking layer, said that at 17:29 Beijing time on October 31, roughly 97 million CORE tokens staked through its protocol were withdrawn without authorization and transferred to an attacker's address. The protocol said it immediately paused the affected contracts and is working with the Core team, security partners and exchanges to trace the funds and coordinate freezes and recovery.
Core DAO said the vulnerability affecting b14g does not affect the Core network itself: consensus, validators and staking contracts ran normally throughout, and CORE staked directly with validators or through other protocols is unaffected. Tracking shows about 68 million CORE is still on the Core chain, with exchanges having frozen roughly 9 million CORE tied to the incident.
CryptoSlate reported that "zero-token withdrawals" allowed the attacker to drain the CORE from the Bitcoin staking platform. Recovery is still in progress: the roughly 9 million CORE frozen by exchanges is a partial amount, and the majority of the funds remains on-chain rather than recovered.

entry.title: Two cross-chain bridges in the SOON ecosystem see abnormal withdrawals; officials suspend service and open investigation
entry.summary:
SOON Foundation said that at roughly 11:00 UTC on 31 October 2026, abnormal withdrawal activity occurred on the svmBNB and SOON Mainnet cross-chain bridges. The foundation detected the anomaly at 14:00 UTC that day and immediately shut down the bridging services, saying both bridges remain under its control and will stay offline pending an investigation.
The halt freezes cross-chain movement between svmBNB and SOON Mainnet while the foundation investigates, leaving users unable to bridge assets through either route.
The announcement did not disclose the scale of assets involved in the abnormal withdrawals or any specific losses. SOON said it will publish further information as the investigation progresses.

entry.title: Coinbase's Third-Party Vendor Problem Strikes Again With Amplitude Leak
entry.summary:
Coinbase acknowledged a security incident at Amplitude, its third-party product analytics provider, which exposed contact information belonging to a small subset of Coinbase customers alongside other Amplitude customers. Coinbase says its own platform was not breached, and the company has pushed back on circulating claims that 70,000 users were affected.
The incident extends a pattern the source headline frames as recurring for Coinbase: customer data leaving the exchange through outside vendors rather than through a breach of Coinbase's own systems. Exposed contact details give attackers material for phishing and social-engineering attempts aimed at exchange users.
According to The CyberSec Guru, Coinbase disclosed the Amplitude incident on October 28. Reporting also notes that Coinbase's position is that it "has not had a data breach," with the impact attributed to Amplitude and limited to a small subset of customer contact data.

entry.title: Bitcoin redemption freeze puts $136 million Aave market under scrutiny
entry.summary:
A freeze on Bitcoin redemptions has put an Aave lending market holding roughly $136 million in exposure under scrutiny, according to CryptoSlate. The halt raises questions about the solvency of the Bitcoin-pegged asset's issuer and the quality of collateral backing that market.
If holders of the affected Bitcoin-pegged asset cannot redeem it for native BTC, the collateral backing loans on that Aave market may be worth less than its on-chain price implies, exposing lenders on that market to potential shortfalls.
The $136 million figure refers to the size of the Aave market's exposure, not a confirmed loss. The freeze concerns redemption of a Bitcoin-pegged token used as collateral rather than a failure of Aave itself.

entry.title: NXTT Plans to Sell or Collateralize 5,833 Bitcoin Worth About $449 Million
entry.summary:
Next Technology Holding (NXTT), a Nasdaq-listed software company, said its board has authorized the phased sale or collateralization of roughly 5,833 bitcoin, worth about $449 million. The company cited exchange vulnerabilities, including the Binance attack, and the potential threat quantum computing poses to Bitcoin's cryptography, with CEO Weihong Liu to decide the timing, pricing and size of any transactions.
A Nasdaq-listed corporate treasury publicly citing exchange counterparty risk and quantum risk as grounds to sell or pledge its bitcoin marks a notable shift in how corporate holders frame custody risk. The company said the authorization does not guarantee that any transactions will be completed.
NXTT said its bitcoin is not held at or through Binance, and the authorization covers exchange sales, privately negotiated transactions and bitcoin-collateralized financing. Most of the holdings came from a March 2025 deal in which it acquired 5,000 BTC for total consideration of $158.1 million, about $31,600 per coin, paid in shares, warrants and a cash prepayment.

entry.title: U.S. Spot Ethereum ETFs Hit Record 23-Day Net Outflow Streak Since Launch
entry.summary:
Glassnode reported that U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs have posted 23 consecutive trading days of net outflows, their longest such streak since the funds launched. The on-chain analytics firm said the sustained withdrawals point to weakening demand from traditional-finance investors.
Glassnode linked the streak to a pullback by traditional-finance investors who had accumulated ETH heavily in August and September, making the flow data a gauge of institutional appetite for ether exposure.
A net outflow means redemptions from the funds exceeded new share creation on those trading days, so capital was leaving the ETFs rather than entering them.
